A release about the library reading what the files actually say — and about reaching things faster.
Built on [MangoTile 1.0.3](https://github.com/Diffechento/MangoTile/releases/tag/v1.0.3).

**An album is its tags, not its folder.** One record split across two folders — a CD1/CD2 rip, a track
downloaded later into a different place — showed as two albums, because the id the library grouped by
was Android's own, and Android bakes the file's folder into it whenever there is no album artist tag.
Albums are now gathered by what the files say: the album title, plus the album artist where there is
one, so two records that merely share a name ("Greatest Hits") still stay apart. The listening history
follows its albums across the change, and files with no album tag at all keep the old per-folder
behaviour — with no tag there is nothing better to go on.

**A record is filed under its album artist.** A compilation used to live under whoever its first track
happened to credit, and a record where every song reads "band feat. somebody" was by the band and said
so nowhere. The album artist tag is read now — the album's row, its page and whose page it appears on
all follow it, while the credit under each song stays exactly as the file spells it. "Various Artists"
is somewhere to go rather than a name with nothing behind it. A switch on settings → library; needs
Android 11, which is where the system started reporting the tag.

**Drag the left edge of a long list to scroll it fast.** A band down the side of the artists, albums,
songs and genres: put a finger on it and the list travels its whole length under the drag, with the
letter you have reached carried in a tile beside your finger — the gallery movement, on a library. It
appears on lists longer than about two screens; tapping a row inside the band still plays it, and
swiping sideways there still changes section. On settings → gestures, like every other gesture.

**Search the whole library at once**, from a row at the top of "more". Tapping a section header still
filters that one section — this is the other question, where you do not know whether what you
half-remember is a title, a band or a record. Results come grouped by what they are, with a count on
each group.

**Open an audio file from anywhere else on the phone.** Tapping a song in a file manager, a download
or an attachment offers MetroMusic and plays it, with the player already up. A file the library knows
is played as that track, counted and queued like any other; one from outside plays as itself, and does
not pretend to be part of a library it is not in.

**Even out the volume between tracks**, off by default, on settings → playback. It reads the
ReplayGain tags files are given when they are ripped — ID3, Vorbis comments and MP4 atoms alike, and
the R128 numbers Opus uses — out of the stream the player is already parsing, so it costs nothing and
needs no second pass over the files. It can only turn a loud track down, never a quiet one up, which
is the honest limit of a volume that is a fraction of the output.

**Save the queue as a playlist.** A queue built out of four albums and then pruned is a playlist that
does not exist yet, and the only way to keep it used to be building it again from memory. One button
under the queue's title; the order it writes down is the order on screen.

**Fixed: the banner at the top of the screen arrived in two jerks.** The volume strip, "added to
queue" and "press back again" all drop in from the top edge, and all three did it by moving their own
window — which the system applies on its own schedule, so almost the whole travel happened before
anything was on screen and the last few pixels then crawled. Both halves are gone: the strip is placed
once and its contents drop inside it, clear of the clock. That is framework work — MangoTile 1.0.3.

**Fixed: the player did not open when the app was launched to play something.** Nothing had a track
for the first moment of a launch, and that counted as the queue having been lost, which closes the
player. It only counts as lost once something has actually played.

---

Scrobbling, the lyrics, the online cover lookup and the equalizer are unchanged. The APK carries the
same signing certificate as every release since 1.0 (`SHA-256 494018a9…2acf7c09`), so it installs over
any of them as an update and keeps your settings, favourites, play counts and queue.

minSdk 26 · compileSdk 36 · GPLv3 · third-party notices are in the app, on settings → about.
